goal: Make block-I/O error handling consistent so disk failures are surfaced instead of silently leaving the node stuck or crashing
Fixes cases where a node appears healthy but can no longer advance the chain, or crashes via asserts on disk errors
reviewability: Paused: an Approach NACK on the core error-handling design is unresolved and unanswered for 69 days
Further code review risks being invalidated by a change in direction, wait for resolution
agreement: Disputed: a formal Approach NACK on the core design remains unresolved despite the author's defense (josibake)
Author defended the current approach but did not change the code (furszy)
An unanswered meta-question asks whether this fix approach should be pursued at all or folded into a larger coordinated PR (maflcko)
Six reviewers gave favorable ACKs on earlier revisions, but the later NACK supersedes that consensus for merge readiness (l0rinc, maflcko, rkrux, w0xlt, frankomosh, sedited)

categories.name: validation
why: P1 because it fixes a serious reliability failure where the node stays alive but stuck, repeatedly failing to advance the chain
The prior behavior only logged at debug level, so most users would never notice the node had stalled
This is a real reliability fix independent of the unresolved design dispute

categories.name: p2p
why: P2 because it fixes real inconsistencies in how P2P requests respond to block I/O errors
GETDATA now disconnects the peer and GETBLOCKTXN triggers a fatal shutdown instead of an assert or silent drop
Benefits node operators and peers by making failure behavior predictable instead of silent or crashy

categories.name: indexes
why: P3 because it removes one crash scenario for indexes but is explicitly an incomplete interim fix
Reviewers note it may just shift from crashing to silently ignoring errors on non-p2p paths
Proper index error handling is acknowledged as a separate follow-up

categories.name: tests
why: P3 because most of the large test addition pins area-specific behavior rather than extending the test framework
The new SimulateFileSystemError helper is a reusable capability that a reviewer suggested generalizing further
Marginal on its own since the value is mostly in the test framework helper rather than the many pinning tests
